identity.name: Caustic sulfite caramel
identity.chemical_class: Class II caramel colour (sulfite process caramel)

function.mechanism: Controlled heat processing of carbohydrates (with sulfite and alkali reagents for Class II) forms complex coloured compounds that impart brown colour in foods.

adi.basis: EFSA 2011 re-evaluation established a group ADI for caramel colours (E150a,b,c,d); class II exposure estimates were below ADI in that opinion.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported class II (E150b) exposure estimates below ADI; concern in that opinion focused more on other classes and certain constituents (e.g., THI in class III).

fda.notes: 21 CFR 73.85 authorizes caramel as a color additive for foods generally at GMP; 21 CFR 182.1235 lists caramel as GRAS under GMP.

adi.basis: JECFA/WHO entry for caustic sulfite caramel (Class II) lists ADI 0-160 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: IARC classifies 4-methylimidazole (a related caramel-process contaminant context) as Group 2B; this is a broader caramel-colour concern rather than a direct E150b monograph classification.
Recent high-dose animal 4-MEI studies report acute neurobehavioral toxicity signals, indicating potential hazard at sufficiently high doses.
Reproductive-related effects are reported in some 4-MEI animal models, but exposure-based risk assessments at current U.S. dietary levels reported MOEs >100 and low concern.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2011 caramel-colour re-evaluation reported class II (E150b) exposure estimates below ADI.
WHO/JECFA maintains ADI 0-160 mg/kg bw for caustic sulfite caramel (Class II).
A 2025 reproductive/developmental risk assessment for 4-MEI reported margins of exposure above commonly used concern thresholds for U.S. dietary exposure scenarios.

adi_exceedance.notes: Within the EFSA 2011 re-evaluation context, class II exposure was below ADI; exceedance concerns in that opinion were not centered on class II.

risk_assessment.rationale: E150b is approved by EFSA/FDA and evaluated by JECFA with explicit ADI values and no direct IARC classification for E150b itself. Existing concern signals are mainly from related contaminant literature (not direct class-II-specific harm at regulated intake levels).
key_factors: EFSA group ADI framework with class II exposure below ADI in the 2011 opinion
JECFA ADI 0-160 mg/kg bw for class II
U.S. CFR authorization under 21 CFR 73.85 and GRAS listing of caramel in 21 CFR 182.1235
No direct IARC classification for E150b
Recent toxicology concern literature is primarily 4-MEI-focused and not directly equivalent to E150b exposure
